arxiv-1411-1538.title: Direction for the Future – Successive Acceleration of Positive and Negative Ions Applied to Space Propulsion
arxiv-1411-1538.creator: A. Aanesland, J. Bredin, L. Popelier and P. Chabert
arxiv-1411-1538.description: Abstract Electrical space thrusters show important advantages for applications in outer space compared to chemical thrusters, as they allow a longer mission lifetime with lower weight and propellant consumption. Mature technologies on the market today accelerate positive ions to generate thrust.

arxiv-1607-06257.creator: Anton Petrunin ★ ” This work was done while we enjoyed our stay at the MPI Leipzig and finished during a joint week at the IHES. and Wilderich Tuschmann ★
arxiv-1607-06257.description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Anton Petrunin ★ ” This work was done while we enjoyed our stay at the MPI Leipzig and finished during a joint week at the IHES. and Wilderich Tuschmann ★. We investigate asymptotically flat manifolds with cone structure at infinity.

arxiv-1904-05546.title: A volumetric framework for quantum computer benchmarks
arxiv-1904-05546.creator: Robin Blume-Kohout, Kevin Young
arxiv-1904-05546.description: Abstract We propose a very large family of benchmarks for probing the performance of quantum computers. We call them volumetric benchmarks (VBs) because they generalize IBM’s benchmark for measuring quantum volume [ 1 ] . The quantum volume benchmark defines a family of square circuits whose depth d d and width w w are the same.

arxiv-2204-07021.title: On Measuring Model Complexity in Heteroscedastic Linear Regression
arxiv-2204-07021.creator: Bo Luan, Yoonkyung Lee, Yunzhang Zhu
arxiv-2204-07021.description: Abstract Heteroscedasticity is common in real world applications and is often handled by incorporating case weights into a modeling procedure. Intuitively, models fitted with different weight schemes would have a different level of complexity depending on how well the weights match the inverse of error variances.

arxiv-2303-01281.title: Relative homological algebra for bivariant K-theory Thanks: Supported by Shota Rustaveli National Science Foundation of Georgia, FR-18-10849. Thanks: George Nadareishvili, A. Razmadze Mathematical Institute, gnadare@gwdg.de
arxiv-2303-01281.creator: George Nadareishvili
arxiv-2303-01281.description: Abstract . This survey article on relative homological algebra in bivariant K-thoery is mainly intended for readers with a background knowledge in triangulated categories. We briefly recall the general theory of relative homological algebra in triangulated categories and latter specialize it to the non-equivariant and the equivariant bivariant K-thoery, where the actions on C*-algebras is by a finite cyclic group.

arxiv-2304-05897.title: Hydrogen-free Wolf-Rayet stars: Helium stars with envelope-inflation structure and rotation
arxiv-2304-05897.creator: Xizhen Lu, Chunhua Zhu, Helei Liu, Sufen Guo, Jinlong Yu, Guoliang Lü
arxiv-2304-05897.description: Abstract Context. Observations have shown that the effective temperature of hydrogen-free Wolf-Rayet (WR) stars is considerably lower than that of the standard model, which means that the radius of the observed H-free WR stars is several times larger than that estimated by the standard model.

arxiv-2305-17886.title: Action valuation of on- and off-ball soccer players based on multi-agent deep reinforcement learning
arxiv-2305-17886.creator: Hiroshi Nakahara, Kazushi Tsutsui, Kazuya Takeda, Keisuke Fujii
arxiv-2305-17886.description: Abstract Analysis of invasive sports such as soccer is challenging because the game situation changes continuously in time and space, and multiple agents individually recognize the game situation and make decisions. Previous studies using deep reinforcement learning have often considered teams as a single agent and valued the teams and players who hold the ball in each discrete event.

arxiv-2310-02587.title: On R R -matrix formulation of q ​ q qq -characters
arxiv-2310-02587.creator: Mehmet Batu Bayındırlı, Dilan Nur Demirtaş, Can Kozçaz, Yegor Zenkevich
arxiv-2310-02587.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mehmet Batu Bayındırlı, Dilan Nur Demirtaş, Can Kozçaz, Yegor Zenkevich. We introduce an R R -matrix formulation of q ​ q qq -characters and corresponding Frenkel-Reshetikhin deformed W W -algebras. The R R -matrix featuring in the construction is of Ding-Iohara-Miki (DIM) algebra, while the type of the q ​ q qq -character is determined by the network of Fock representations corresponding to a web of 5-branes geometrically engineering a quiver gauge theory.

arxiv-2403-11715.title: Combination and Reinterpretation of LHC SUSY Searches
arxiv-2403-11715.creator: Alexander Feike, ​​, Juri Fiaschi, ​​, Benjamin Fuks, ​​, Michael Klasen, and Alexander Puck Neuwirth
arxiv-2403-11715.description: Abstract To maximise the information obtained from various independent new physics searches conducted at the LHC, it is imperative to consider the combination of multiple analyses. To showcase the exclusion power gained by combining signal regions from different searches, we consider a simplified scenario inspired by supersymmetry, with all particles but one squark flavour and a bino-like neutralino decoupled.

arxiv-2510-19426.title: Using did_multiplegt_dyn to Estimate Event-Study Effects in Complex Designs: Overview, and Four Examples Based on Real Datasets Thanks: Chaisemartin, Ciccia, Knau, Malézieux, and Sow wrote the Stata package. Angotti, Ciccia, Fabre, and Quispe translated it into R. Arboleda and Knau ran the simulatio
arxiv-2510-19426.creator: Clément de Chaisemartin, Diego Ciccia, Felix Knau, Mélitine Malézieux, Doulo Sow, David Arboleda, Romain Angotti, Xavier D’Haultfœuille, Bingxue Li, Henri Fabre, Anzony Quispe
arxiv-2510-19426.description: Abstract The command did_multiplegt_dyn can be used to estimate event-study effects in complex designs with a potentially non-binary and/or non-absorbing treatment. This paper starts by providing an overview of the estimators computed by the command. Then, simulations based on three real datasets are used to demonstrate the estimators’ properties.

arxiv-2511-20733.title: InvisibleBench: A Deployment Gate for Caregiving Relationship AI
arxiv-2511-20733.creator: Ali Madad
arxiv-2511-20733.description: Abstract InvisibleBench is a deployment gate for caregiving relationship AI, evaluating 3–20+ turn conversations across five dimensions (Safety, Compliance, Trauma-Informed Design, Belonging & Cultural Fitness, Memory) with autofails for missed crises, medical advice (WOPR Act), harmful information, and attachment engineering. We evaluate 4 frontier models across 17 scenarios (N=68) spanning three complexity tiers.

pmc-10531612.title: Epidemiology and Long-Term Outcomes in Thoracic Transplantation
pmc-10531612.creator: Abey S Abraham, Manila Singh, Matthew S Abraham, Sanchit Ahuja, Louise Y Sun, Matthew Vanneman
pmc-10531612.description: Over the past five decades, outcomes for lung transplantation have significantly improved in the early post-operative period, such that lung transplant is now the gold standard treatment for end-stage respiratory disease. The major limitation that impacts lung transplant survival rates is the development of chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD).

pmc-10547781.title: Human papillomavirus and prostate cancer: systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-10547781.creator: Irina A. Tsydenova, Marina K. Ibragimova, Matvey M. Tsyganov, Nikolai V. Litviakov
pmc-10547781.description: The involvement of human papillomavirus (HPV) in the prostate carcinogenesis is a controversial issue. The presented meta-analysis was carried out to systematize the currently available research results regarding this question. The meta-analysis includes case–control studies from 1991 to 2022, which were collected from publicly available bibliometric databases. The meta-analysis was performed using Meta-Essentials_1.5 software.

pmc-10594305.title: Premature termination, satisfaction with care, and shared decision-making during home treatment compared to inpatient treatment: A quasi-experimental trial
pmc-10594305.creator: Stefan Weinmann, Konstantinos Nikolaidis, Gerhard Längle, Sebastian von Peter, Peter Brieger, Jürgen Timm, Lasse Fischer, Svenja Raschmann, Martin Holzke, Julian Schwarz, Luisa Klocke, Sandeep Rout, Constanze Hirschmeier, Uwe Herwig, Janina Richter, Reinhold Kilian, Johanna Baumgardt, Johannes Haman
pmc-10594305.description: BackgroundInpatient equivalent home treatment (IEHT), implemented in Germany since 2018, is a specific form of home treatment. Between 2021 and 2022, IEHT was compared to inpatient psychiatric treatment in a 12-months follow-up quasi-experimental study with two propensity score matched cohorts in 10 psychiatric centers in Germany.

pmc-10654630.title: Unveiling the novel immune and molecular signatures of ovarian cancer: insights and innovations from single-cell sequencing
pmc-10654630.creator: Zhongkang Li, Haihan Gu, Xiaotong Xu, Yanpeng Tian, Xianghua Huang, Yanfang Du
pmc-10654630.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Ovarian cancer is a highly heterogeneous and lethal malignancy with limited treatment options. Over the past decade, single-cell sequencing has emerged as an advanced biological technology capable of decoding the landscape of ovarian cancer at the single-cell resolution. It operates at the level of genes, transcriptomes, proteins, epigenomes, and metabolisms, providing detailed information that is distinct from bulk sequencing methods, which only offer average data for specific lesions.

pmc-11506347.title: Antibody-Based Therapies for Peripheral T-Cell Lymphoma
pmc-11506347.creator: Nazila Shafagati, Suman Paul, Sima Rozati, Cole H Sterling
pmc-11506347.description: Simple SummaryPeripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL) is a collection of aggressive malignancies with poor long-term survival and limited effective treatment options. Despite unique challenges associated with identifying and targeting malignant T-cell antigens, the use of antibody-based therapies holds great potential. Here, we review the current and future roles of antibody-based therapies for PTCL.

pmc-12441302.title: Influence of Gamma Irradiation and Antioxidants on the Quality of Spicy Chicken Meat During Refrigerated Storage
pmc-12441302.creator: Guolin Li, Ping Lin, Yangbo He, Zhihui Liu, Yongfu Li
pmc-12441302.description: The effects of antioxidants on microbial quality, color, lipid oxidation, fatty acids, odor, and volatile compounds in irradiated spicy chicken were investigated. Chicken meat was treated with antioxidants (α‐tocopherol, phytic acid, tea polyphenols, and tertiary butydroquinone) and 4 kGy gamma irradiation.

pmc-12658391.title: Behavioral Profiles and Sociodemographic Predictors of Planetary Health Diet Engagement Among Health Care Professionals to Inform Public Health Promotion: Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-12658391.creator: Florence Carrouel, Rita Nugem, Laurie Fraticelli, Yohan Fayet, Lama Basbous, Corélie Salque, Claude Dussart, Marie-Thérèse Charreyre, Romain Lan, Audrey Murat-ringot, Amaryllis Mavragani, Travis Sanchez, Frederic Denis, Cindy Neuzillet
pmc-12658391.description: BackgroundThe planetary health diet (PHD) promotes dietary habits that are beneficial to human health and environmental sustainability, two closely related goals of modern public health. Health care professionals are expected to lead by example and use their position to encourage their patients and communities to adopt healthier and more sustainable behaviors.

pmc-13080685.title: ALPL Mutations With Dominant‐Negative Effect in Infantile Hypophosphatasia Monozygotic Twins
pmc-13080685.creator: Luna Hao, Na Huang, Yilun Tao, Hui Li, Juyu Zhuang, Xiaoyun Li, Zekun Hao, Feng Zhao, Harleen Khatra
pmc-13080685.description: Background and AimsHypophosphatasia (HPP) is a rare inborn error of metabolism caused by ALPL gene mutations, resulting in deficient tissue‐nonspecific alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity. We investigated genotype–phenotype correlations in a monozygotic female twin pair with infantile HPP.MethodsPeripheral blood samples were collected from two female twins with HPP and their family members.

pmc-13459827.title: Whole-genome sequence of Rahnella aceris HPDA25 isolated from mycorrhizosphere of Gastrodia elata
pmc-13459827.creator: Wenshu Zou, Kangchen Liu, Xiaoai Li, Shuyuan Cheng, Pengjie Han, Honghong Jiao, Zhongyi Hua, Tianrui Liu, Yuan Yuan
pmc-13459827.description: ObjectivesThe growth, development, and accumulation of active compounds in Gastrodia elata are influenced by its mycorrhizosphere bacteria, which indirectly enhances host nutrition by stimulating the growth of the orchid mycorrhizal fungus Armillaria gallica. However, data on the mycorrhizosphere bacterial community of G. elata, especially on key functional strains, remain limited, restricting their application in medicinal plant cultivation.

uslaw-usc-t25-s292a.title: 25 U.S.C. § 292a — Discontinuance of boarding and day schools having small attendance
uslaw-usc-t25-s292a.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t25-s292a.description: United States Code, Title 25 (Indians); Chapter 7 (Education Of Indians). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. All reservation and nonreservation boarding schools with an average attendance in any year of less than forty-five and eighty pupils, respectively, shall be discontinued on or before the beginning of the ensuing fiscal year. The pupils in schools so discontinued shall be transferred first, if possible.

uslaw-usc-t54-s302906.title: 54 U.S.C. § 302906 — Grants and loans to Indian tribes and nonprofit organizations representing ethnic or minority groups
uslaw-usc-t54-s302906.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t54-s302906.description: United States Code, Title 54 (National Park Service And Related Programs); Chapter 3029 (Grants). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The Secretary may, in consultation with the appropriate State Historic Preservation Officer, make grants or loans or both under this subdivision to Indian tribes and to nonprofit organizations representing ethnic or minority groups for the preservation of their cultural heritage.
